title: outage-briefing-with-verified-evidence-and-rollback-actions-2026-09-03
subject_line: Update: September 1 — Verified evidence + rollback options for the inference outage
status_page_update: Summary for public status page: On 2026-09-01 at ~03:40 UTC, a subset of traffic to the hosted inference cluster experienced elevated latency and partial failed responses for 42 minutes. Root cause and mitigations are under investigation; we have a targeted fix and verified data integrity for impacted requests. Services are returned to normal by 04:22 UTC. We're preparing a customer-facing timeline and options for replay or rollback where applicable.
customer_postmortem_summary: Plain-language summary for customers: We identified a cascading resource-starvation condition in our per-tenant routing layer that caused some requests to queue and time out. A controller misconfiguration combined with a late GC cycle on a routing node reduced throughput and triggered emergency fallbacks that returned partial results for some tenants. No customer data was exposed; model outputs themselves were affected for a small percentage of requests. We have validated request logs and can offer targeted replay or a compensating credit. Below are the verified evidence items and next steps you can take.
timeline_bullet_points:
- 2026-09-01 03:38 UTC: Routine autoscaler executed a policy change.
- 2026-09-01 03:40 UTC: Elevated queue lengths and tail latency detected; alerts triggered.
- 2026-09-01 03:43 UTC: Automatic fallback to reduced-capacity model variants for some tenants; customers may have seen shorter or truncated outputs.
- 2026-09-01 04:01 UTC: Engineering isolated a routing node with abnormal memory behavior and removed it from the pool.
- 2026-09-01 04:15 UTC: Controlled rollout of configuration fix to routing tier started.
- 2026-09-01 04:22 UTC: System metrics returned to baseline; streaming and synchronous APIs show normal performance.
technical_root_cause: A latent controller config combining an aggressive scaling cooldown with a routing node GC regression allowed transient memory pressure to accumulate. This produced cascading queueing across several tenant shards and invoked emergency fallbacks. The fallback path produced valid but truncated model outputs for approximately 0.7% of API calls during the window.
mitigation_and_fix: Immediate mitigation: removed the affected routing node and disabled the aggressive cooldown policy while we validated stability. Permanent fix: a configuration guard and a GC patch were applied to the routing node images; the autoscaler cooldown got a conservative upper bound. We added an automated health-check that proactively drains nodes showing increasing queue length ahead of GC. These changes are deployed and monitored in canary and global pools.
customer_actions:
If you believe your tenant was impacted, please reply to this message with the tenant ID(s) or use the self-serve verification tool. Options we can provide:
1) Targeted replay of the request window (customer consent required): we will re-run impacted requests against the same model version and provide the outputs and replay log.
2) Rollback/consistency run: for customers using pinned model versions, we can force-validate that pinned variants behaved as expected and replay with identical routing when possible.
3) Compensation credit: if replay is not accepted, we can offer a credit equivalent to the compute cost of the affected window.
Action checklist: send tenant IDs; preferred option (replay/rollback/credit); contact email; SLA preference for delivery timeframe (24/48/72 hours).
sla_and_compensation: We recognize impact to reliability. For qualifying tenants (those that experienced >0.5% call failure or truncated output during the window), we will: (a) perform a targeted replay within SLA of 48 hours upon consent, or (b) issue a billing credit processed within 7 business days. For enterprise customers with Dedicated contracts, we will coordinate an exec-summary with tailored remedies and an SLA exception if required.

Coordinate with solutions-eng for customers requiring replay support. Add a short statuspage follow-up that links to the full postmortem once finalized.
qa_notes: Run the verification script linked in artifacts to confirm per-tenant call counts. Confirm that the replay process is idempotent for side-effecting integrations; include guidance for partners with external webhooks.
communication_plan: 1) Short statuspage update published (public) — done. 2) Tiered customer emails: critical tenants first (today), broader customer note with replay choices (within 24 hours). 3) Postmortem published to customers and Confluence (within 72 hours). 4) Follow-up surveys for customers who opt into replay to capture any divergence.
